completed_checkpoints.conclusion: BOOT.BIN is the probable high-level save-interface owner, with four exact-binary guarded static entry-point candidates. Serializer, checksum, slot, recovery, and exclusive module-ownership semantics remain unresolved.

Two BOOT.BIN controllers construct the same 0x600-byte PSP savedata parameter block. The serialized Fight Night payload is separate and crosses the operating-system utility boundary through pointer, capacity, and active-size fields at offsets 0x74, 0x78, and 0x7C. The callback owner, data-flow direction, serializer and deserializer sets, checksum, and payload field meanings remain unresolved.

next_question: Resolve the indirect payload-provider callback target and owner, then distinguish serializer and deserializer directions without assigning persistent field meanings prematurely.
